'''Adrian Ioana''' (born 18 January 1981, [[Târgu Jiu]]) is a Romanian mathematician.<ref name=vita>{{cite web |url=http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~aioana/cv.pdf |title=Adrian Ioana CV|website=math.ucsd.edu|access-date=9 April 2023}}</ref> He is currently a professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]].

Ioana earned a BS in Mathematics from the [[University of Bucharest]] in 2003, and completed his PhD at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 2007, under the supervision of [[Sorin Popa]].  He then was a postdoc at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and a Research Fellow supported by the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]], after which he joined UC San Diego in 2011.<ref name="vita"/>

For his contributions to [[von Neumann algebras]] and [[representation theory]] of [[Group (mathematics)|groups]], he was awarded a 2012 [[EMS Prize]]. In 2018 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in Rio de Janeiro (on "Rigidity for von Neumann algebras").
